blocks.name: Structure of silicon(IV) oxide
blocks.definition: Describe the giant covalent structure of silicon(IV) oxide, SiO2

blocks.text: What is the structure of silicon(IV) oxide?

blocks.md:
- Silicon(IV) oxide (also known as silicon dioxide or silica), SiO<sub>2</sub>, is a macromolecular compound which occurs naturally as **sand **and **quartz**
- Each oxygen atom forms covalent bonds with **2** silicon atoms and each silicon atom in turn forms covalent bonds with **4** oxygen atoms
- A tetrahedron is formed with one silicon atom and four oxygen atoms, similar to diamond

blocks.name: Comparing diamond & silicon(IV) oxide
blocks.definition: Describe the similarity in properties between diamond and silicon(IV) oxide, related to their structures

blocks.text: How does diamond compare to silicon(IV) oxide?

blocks.md:
- SiO<sub>2</sub> has lots of very strong covalent bonds and no intermolecular forces so it has similar properties to diamond
- It is very **hard**, has a very **high** boiling point, is insoluble in water and does not conduct electricity
- SiO<sub>2</sub> is cheap since it is available naturally and is used to make sandpaper and to line the inside of furnaces
